clue.text: Spar, ultimately, with police — then produce weapon

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters, so the police
to arm is to supply or take up weapons

explanation.surface: Someone at a supermarket called Spar finds the police arriving and pulls out a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' supplies its own last letter, Y; Scotland Yard, the Metropolitan Police headquarters in London, gives YARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is the outer end of a ship's yard, the horizontal spar from which a sail hangs.

clue.text: The old sign used by these signallers

parts.note: ye is the archaic spelling of 'the'
an omen is a portent or sign

explanation.surface: An ancient symbol was the one these signallers adopted.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Royal Navy a yeoman of signals is the rating in charge of flag and lamp signalling.

clue.text: Recall ring-leader — the game is up

indicators.note: the leader of the word ring is its opening letter
in a down clue going up means the game's name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: ecarte is a card game for two players

explanation.surface: A gang boss is told the game is up and the police want him to recall events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is up' reads the card game upwards, as suits a down clue; 'the game is up' looks like a confession.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back over past events in the mind is to recall them.

clue.text: You and I will head south in a van in fearful condition

indicators.note: the pair WE S is placed inside A TRUCK

parts.note: a van is a kind of truck

indicators.note: WE comes at the head of, in front of, the S

parts.note: the two of us together are we

explanation.surface: Two people drive off south in a van, terrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will head' means the pronoun goes in front of the compass letter before both are put into the van.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck with awe means filled with dread or wonder, a frightened state.

clue.text: Evaluation made by certain people; in essence

indicators.note: the words for certain and people go inside the word for essence

parts.note: the meat of something is its essence or substance
sure means certain
men are people

explanation.surface: An assessment carried out by certain people is, at heart, what is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Measuring something is one way of assessing or evaluating it.

clue.text: Interrupt attempt to cover tracks after reverse

indicators.note: once the whole construction is complete it is read backwards
the word for attempt goes round the word for tracks

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
ruts are tracks worn in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hide their trail after a setback, and must not be disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reverse' applies to everything built first, so the whole container is read backwards at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone is to break in on or interrupt them.

clue.text: It's said some precipitation is expected

indicators.note: the word for some precipitation is spoken, and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: dew is moisture that condenses overnight, a form of precipitation

explanation.surface: Forecasters say some rain is on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: A train that is due is expected to arrive.

clue.text: Drain installed in house we rented

indicators.note: the answer is set inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A drainage pipe was fitted in the house we were renting.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer is an underground drain carrying waste water.

clue.text: One fabulous equine creature, or three harnessed together

definitions.meaning: a mythical horse with a single horn
a carriage team of three horses, two abreast with one in front

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the legendary one-horned horse and a team of three horses yoked together.

clue.text: Swimmer is round about 21, separated

indicators.note: the word for swimmer is placed around the word for about

parts.note: a bather is someone swimming
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A swimmer turns about, a player at 21 standing apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is SHORTSTOP; split into two words it becomes 'short stop', which defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief pause for rest is a short stop.

clue.text: Other people with top cards overwhelmed by somebody intent on gain

indicators.note: the first pieces are swallowed up by the word for somebody

parts.note: one means a person, somebody
them refers to other people
ace and king, A and K, are the highest cards

explanation.surface: Other players holding the best cards are beaten by a greedy opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone looking out for profit or advantage is ambitious and self-seeking.

clue.text: Record sound that's heard

indicators.note: the word for sound is spoken aloud to give the answer

parts.note: sound as in valid or correct means right

explanation.surface: Note down a noise someone has picked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' here is the adjective meaning correct, not a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down on paper is to record it.

clue.text: Stick around before opening of theatre's play

indicators.note: the reversed word comes before the next letter
the word for stick is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

indicators.note: the opening of theatre's is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone hangs around before the theatre's play opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the stick backwards; 'play' is a verb here, to act out.
explanation.definitionFit: To act out a part on stage is to play it.

clue.text: Prompt use could be made of this chief

indicators.note: the answer's letters can be rearranged to form the clue's words prompt use

explanation.surface: Something to be put to use promptly is of top importance.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters rearrange to PROMPT USE; 'could be made of this' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Highest in rank or importance is the same as principal or chief.

clue.text: Belief in 12, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 12 across is uppermost

explanation.surface: A belief held in the chief thing, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: IN plus UPPERMOST (12 across), rearranged, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A presumption is something taken to be true, an assumption or belief.

clue.text: Return of youth not required by Pan?

definitions.text: Return of youth not required by Pan?

parts.words: Return of youth not required by Pan?
parts.note: renewed youthfulness, something Peter Pan, the boy who never grew up, would never need

explanation.definitionFit: Becoming young again is a renewal of youth.

clue.text: Frolic of councillor brought about storm in a teacup

indicators.note: the abbreviation for councillor is brought around the other letters
storm is a turbulent upheaval, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A councillor's antics stir up a storm in a teacup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm in' is the anagram signal hiding in the idiom 'storm in a teacup'; 'brought about' wraps the councillor round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a caper is to leap about playfully, to frolic.

clue.text: Cloudy picture of island — stratus's beginning to cover the interior

indicators.note: these letters fill the interior of the island's name

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Scottish Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: the beginning of stratus's is its first letter

parts.note: to cap is to cover the top of something

explanation.surface: A painting of a Scottish island shows low stratus cloud spreading over its interior.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides; 'the interior' says the new letters fill its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of the sky, often full of clouds, is a skyscape.

clue.text: Those cleaning up joint found offensive weapons

parts.note: a knuckle is a finger joint
dusters are cloths used for cleaning

explanation.surface: The cleaners at a dive discovered some nasty weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a seedy bar, but it is a finger joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal grips worn over the fingers to strengthen a punch are weapons designed for attack.

clue.text: Posh hat seen on an idealist

parts.note: U denotes upper-class usage, so posh
a topi is a sun helmet, a pith hat

explanation.surface: A dreamer is spotted wearing a smart hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes in an ideal society is a visionary idealist.

clue.text: Enrolled in engineers, soldiers start to suffer regret

indicators.note: the soldiers and the letter join the ranks of the engineers' corps

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: the start of suffer is its first letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers who signed up with the engineers soon begin to suffer remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a British Army corps; OR, other ranks, is ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep sorrow for a wrong done is regret, contrition.

clue.text: Writer holding on to money? Only just

indicators.note: the writer's name holds the money symbol inside it

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist
L stands for pound, from Latin libra, so money

explanation.surface: An author clutches his cash, barely managing.
explanation.walkthrough: L for pound goes inside HARDY, the English novelist Thomas Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly means barely or scarcely.

clue.text: Baseball player in pants and jumper, perhaps

parts.note: pants can mean short trousers or shorts
a jumper (a British word for a sweater) is one kind of top

explanation.surface: A ballplayer wearing shorts and a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortstop is the baseball fielder stationed between second and third base.

clue.text: It may symbolise one for a digital computer

definitions.text: It may symbolise one for a digital computer

parts.words: It may symbolise one for a digital computer
parts.note: someone counting on their fingers, digitally, may hold up a single digit to stand for the number one

explanation.definitionFit: The stubby first digit of the hand is raised to show one when counting on fingers.

clue.text: Butterfly, in a word

definitions.meaning: an orange-brown butterfly with a white mark on its wing
the punctuation mark printed after Butterfly in this very clue, named in a word

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a butterfly with a white mark on its underwing and to the punctuation mark printed in the clue.

clue.text: Advertisement that's accepted by society for so long

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
U marks upper-class usage, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: An advert that society approves of runs for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are farewells, ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Was Captain Singleton initially made to be salt?

indicators.note: the initial letter of Singleton is taken

parts.note: kippered fish is cured, preserved in salt and smoked

explanation.surface: Was Defoe's Captain Singleton made into an old salt?
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Singleton is Defoe's pirate novel; 'salt' looks like a sailor but means salted.
explanation.definitionFit: To skipper a ship is to command it as its captain.

clue.text: Woman who's succeeded Ambassador

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: The woman who has taken over as ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun for a female person stands for a woman.

clue.text: Raise opposing card-players by a fraction of a pound, originally

parts.note: at bridge East and North sit as opponents

parts.words: a fraction of a pound, originally
parts.note: the noble was an old English gold coin worth a third of a pound

explanation.surface: Bridge opponents raise the stakes by a few pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to elevate them to the peerage, to raise them.

clue.text: Railwaymen mostly see railway as growth area

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen

indicators.note: most of the word see is kept, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Rail workers regard the railway as a growth sector.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where young plants are grown.
